title: Jallah Town residents reportedly protest electricity supply
location: Jallah Town, Monrovia (reported in search-result excerpts)
participants_original: FrontPage Africa and Global News Network Liberia search-result excerpts say hundreds; exact attendance and independent sourcing are unverified.
threshold_50_evidence: Pending body review. One search-result excerpt uses “hundreds”; a substantially overlapping GNN excerpt is not independent corroboration. The attendance, context, and physical occurrence remain unverified.

occurrence_and_date.summary: Search-result excerpts report a Jallah Town electricity protest on February 8, 2021. Neither article body was read; physical occurrence and date remain provisional.

location_and_demand.summary: The excerpts identify Jallah Town and electricity supply as the reported grievance. The exact demand and whether it was directed to the Liberian state are unverified.

participants.summary: Search-result excerpts report “hundreds”; no article body, count method, or independent corroboration is available.

notes: Discovery lead only. This is the February-owned Jallah Town lead also preserved as outside-month item LBR202101-X003; it is not a second event. FrontPage Africa and GNN excerpts substantially overlap, and GNN is a March follow-up; do not count them as independent confirmation. The headline’s word “violent” is not enough to code protester violence. No event end or response is established.
open_questions: Did the public gathering occur as reported, and was February 8 its physical start date?
How many people assembled simultaneously, and does reliable evidence establish at least 50?
What exact electricity demand was made, and was it directed to the Liberian state or a state policy?
Are the FrontPage Africa and GNN accounts independent, or is either derived from the other?
Was any violence or state response tied to this gathering?
When did the gathering physically end?

title: Public Workers Consortium press conference reportedly announces warning strikes
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. The search-result excerpt calls this a press conference but gives no physical attendance count or adequate crowd description.

occurrence_and_date.summary: A February 13 search-result header and excerpt report a Public Workers Consortium press conference in Monrovia on February 10. The article body was inaccessible; date and occurrence remain provisional.

organizer_and_location.summary: The excerpt names the Public Workers Consortium and Monrovia; neither detail was checked in the article body.

reported_grievance.summary: The excerpt refers to salary deductions, retirement, and other grievances. Exact demands and whether they targeted state policy or the state as employer remain unverified.

participants.summary: No attendance count or sufficient description of the number assembled appears in the saved search-result excerpt.

notes: The reported press conference is a discovery lead, not a verified qualifying gathering. Demands are left uncategorized because the precise grievance and state target are not established. The future warning strikes are not treated as executed events; see LBR202102-X002.
open_questions: Did the press conference occur on February 10, and how many people physically attended?
Were the grievances demands to the Liberian state or public employer, and what were their exact terms?
Did any warning strike actually occur during February 2021?
What were the physical start/end, protester conduct, and any state response?
